flags: minor: choices A and D are implausible as intercept interpretations (A restates a rate, D is nonsensical $135/hour), so the item is effectively a two-way choice between B and C
Q027-01.notes: x-intercept: y=0, 15x=135, x=9 -> 9 hours at job A, none at B. C swaps the jobs.

flags: minor: D (4.5(n+p)=87) is weak; with n+p=40 it gives 180=87, an inconsistent system, so it is easily eliminated
Q027-02.notes: Count: n+p=40; cost: 3n+1.5p=87. Consistent solution n=18, p=22. A swaps totals, B swaps prices.

Q027-03.notes: Product of roots = c/a = -12/2 = -6. Discriminant k^2+96>0 for every k, so the 'two real solutions' condition always holds; the answer does not depend on k. Needs Vieta (or test k=0: x^2=6, product -6).

Q027-04.notes: (x+1)^2=9 -> x+1=+/-3 -> x=2 or x=-4. B is the sign-error trap (x-1=+/-3); A misreads vertex values; C uses +/-9. Graphing makes it quick.

Q027-05.notes: f(x-2)+3 shifts the vertex (0,0) right 2, up 3 -> (2,3). A and B are sign-error distractors, D swaps coordinates.

Q027-06.notes: a+3=12 -> a=9; ab=18 -> b=2. The x>1 condition makes exponent matching valid. Two routine steps.

Q027-07.notes: 6^2+y^2=100, y=8 (Quadrant I). tan = y/x = 8/6 = 4/3. 3/4 is the reciprocal trap; 3/5 and 4/5 are cos and sin.
